title: Relocate closed-world scope to packet-and-layer metadata
description:
Relocate closed-world scope from positive annotations into reviewed packet-and-layer metadata.

Today scope exists only as `expected.exhaustive_scope_files` repeated across **434 positive annotations**, totalling roughly 18,900 entries with heavy duplication. Moving it is a real migration with a dedup and review-provenance step, not a schema rename.

It also removes the current failure the decision calls out: a layer reviewed exhaustively but containing no positives declares no scope at all and therefore cannot catch hallucinated findings.

Note for the baseline: once precision scope becomes reviewed scope intersected with successfully processed files, the scope lists are dominated by `.php` (~6,500 entries) and `.rb` (~6,000) that ingest cannot open.

Startable now — independent of the gate rulings.
